hypothesis: At least one calibrated non-Gaussian residual mechanism improves held-out rare-tail predictive transfer or interval calibration over the existing Gaussian baseline without reducing overall transfer/driver floors or exceeding the charged artifact cap; global MSE improvement alone is insufficient.

estimand.primary: paired change in lower-tail query loss and 50/80/90 percent predictive-interval coverage on the same untouched source and query rows
estimand.threshold_status: aspirational_working_defaults_only; contracts/tdl-contract-v1.json remains authoritative and unfrozen

source.rule: admit two independent source families with verified rights and lineage; keep each source family, all patients/entities, and its latest time block intact in the final query holdout; no source or query row may enter fit, residual fitting, selection, or calibration

model.rule: freeze exact adapter, learner, dependency, and checkpoint digests before opening source holdouts; all residual candidates score the same query rows and model identities

rare_slices: each categorical level with fit prevalence at most 5 percent
outer-fit reference residual lower and upper deciles
target lower and upper deciles, with boundaries estimated on fit rows only

pilot.fixture: compiler-inline deterministic residual mechanism fixture, 96 rows, one feature, fixed seed 1729
pilot.purpose: price compatibility and deterministic mechanism construction only; not external scientific evidence

study_design.stop_rule: Stop the study and retain the failed/unsupported receipt if any critical slice misses its support floor, interval coverage error exceeds 0.05, rare-tail transfer LCB is below 0.8, rare-tail loss exceeds 1.1 times the real-fit reference, overall transfer LCB is below 0.9, driver fidelity LCB is below 0.8, or any artifact exceeds 10240 bytes. No global MSE improvement can override a critical-tail failure. Do not retry an unchanged expensive candidate.

result.evidence: No external source/model holdouts were opened and no candidate is admitted. The deterministic fixture checks compatibility and stop-rule behavior only.
